title: Arcs, Sectors and Areas of Plane Shapes
seo_title: Lengths and Areas – SSS 1 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Find perimeters and areas of plane shapes; find arc lengths, perimeters and areas of sectors and segments of circles. (summary of the NERDC SSS 1 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free SSS 1 maths worksheets on mensuration of plane shapes: circles, arc length, sectors, segments and perimeters. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A sector is a slice of a circle; its angle θ is a fraction θ/360 of the full turn.
  • Arc length = θ/360 × 2πr; sector area = θ/360 × πr².
  • A segment = sector − triangle.

Examples

Example

r = 7 cm, θ = 90°

90/360 × 2 × 22/7 × 7

Answer: Arc = 11 cm

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Using the diameter as the radiusHalve the diameter first.
Leaving out the two radii in the perimeterPerimeter = arc + 2r.
Using 2πr for areaArea uses πr².

faq.a: Use 22/7 or 3.142 as the question says.

items.q: A wheel has a diameter of 84 cm. How far does it travel in 25 complete revolutions? (Use π = 22/7.)
items.e: One revolution = πd = 22/7 × 84 = 264 cm. 25 revolutions = 6,600 cm = 66 m.

A sector of radius 8 cm has arc length 43π cm. What is the angle of the sector?
items.e: θ/360 × 16π = 43π cm. So θ = 360 × 43 ÷ 16 = 30°.

items.q: A sector of radius 5 cm has area 256π cm². What is the angle of the sector?
items.e: θ/360 × 25π = 256π cm². So θ = 360 × 256 ÷ 25 = 60°.

items.q: Find the perimeter of the sector. Give your answer to 1 decimal place.
items.e: Arc = 11.8 cm. Perimeter = arc + 2 radii = 11.8 + 10 = 21.8 cm.

items.e: Arc = 31.4 cm. Perimeter = arc + 2 radii = 31.4 + 12 = 43.4 cm.

items.q: A chord of a circle of radius 15 cm subtends an angle of 60° at the centre. Find the area of the major segment. (Use π = 3.14, √3 = 1.73.)
items.e: Minor segment = 117.75 cm² − 97.31 cm² = 20.44 cm². Major segment = πr² − minor = 706.5 cm² − 20.44 cm² = 686.06 cm².

items.q: A chord of a circle of radius 15 cm subtends an angle of 60° at the centre. Find the area of the minor segment. (Use π = 3.14, √3 = 1.73.)
items.e: Segment = sector − triangle = 117.75 cm² − 97.31 cm² ((√3/4) × 15²) = 20.44 cm².

items.q: A chord of a circle of radius 20 cm subtends an angle of 60° at the centre. Find the area of the minor segment. (Use π = 3.14, √3 = 1.73.)
items.e: Segment = sector − triangle = 209.33 cm² − 173 cm² ((√3/4) × 20²) = 36.33 cm².

items.q: A chord of a circle of radius 28 cm subtends an angle of 60° at the centre. Find the area of the minor segment. (Use π = 3.14, √3 = 1.73.)
items.e: Segment = sector − triangle = 410.29 cm² − 339.08 cm² ((√3/4) × 28²) = 71.21 cm².

items.q: A chord of a circle of radius 10 cm subtends an angle of 90° at the centre. Find the area of the minor segment. (Use π = 3.14.)
items.e: Segment = sector − triangle = 78.5 cm² − 50 cm² (½ × 10 × 10) = 28.5 cm².

items.q: A chord of a circle of radius 14 cm subtends an angle of 60° at the centre. Find the area of the minor segment. (Use π = 3.14, √3 = 1.73.)
items.e: Segment = sector − triangle = 102.57 cm² − 84.77 cm² ((√3/4) × 14²) = 17.8 cm².

items.q: A chord of a circle of radius 12 cm subtends an angle of 90° at the centre. Find the area of the minor segment. (Use π = 3.14.)
items.e: Segment = sector − triangle = 113.04 cm² − 72 cm² (½ × 12 × 12) = 41.04 cm².

items.q: A chord of a circle of radius 15 cm subtends an angle of 90° at the centre. Find the area of the major segment. (Use π = 3.14.)
items.e: Minor segment = 176.63 cm² − 112.5 cm² = 64.13 cm². Major segment = πr² − minor = 706.5 cm² − 64.13 cm² = 642.38 cm².

items.q: A chord of a circle of radius 20 cm subtends an angle of 90° at the centre. Find the area of the major segment. (Use π = 3.14.)
items.e: Minor segment = 314 cm² − 200 cm² = 114 cm². Major segment = πr² − minor = 1,256 cm² − 114 cm² = 1,142 cm².

items.q: A chord of a circle of radius 15 cm subtends an angle of 90° at the centre. Find the area of the minor segment. (Use π = 3.14.)
items.e: Segment = sector − triangle = 176.63 cm² − 112.5 cm² (½ × 15 × 15) = 64.13 cm².

items.q: A horse is tied to a peg at one corner of a square grass field of side 15 m with a rope 14 m long. Find the area of the field it can graze. (Use π = 3.14.)
items.e: The corner angle is 90°, so it grazes a quadrant: ¼ × 3.14 × 14² = 153.86 m².

items.q: From each corner of a square of side 14 cm, a quadrant of radius 7 cm is cut off. Find the area of the remaining part. (Use π = 22/7.)
items.e: Four quadrants make one full circle of radius 7 cm: 14² − 22/7 × 7² = 42 cm².

A brooch is made of a circle of radius 21 mm divided into 4 equal sectors by 2 diameters. Find the area of each sector. (Use π = 22/7.)
items.e: Each sector is a quarter: ¼ × 22/7 × 21² = 346.5 mm².
